name: intraday_vol_pattern_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: NIFTY exhibits a structural U-shaped intraday volatility pattern driven by institutional order concentration: FIIs and domestic institutions front-load directional orders at the open (09:15-10:00) and close (14:30-15:25), creating algorithmic TWAP/VWAP-driven surges where EMA alignment holds for 30-90 seconds; during lunch (11:30-13:30) institutional desks park positions and retail/market-maker activity dominates, so NIFTY drifts in a narrow 30-50 spot pt range and Bollinger Band touches revert reliably because no sustained buy/sell programs are active. When current 3-minute realized vol rises 15%+ above the 30-minute baseline during open/close, the NIFTY order book is in a momentum regime — entries aligned with EMA direction capture the tail of the institutional push. When vol drops 15%+ below baseline during lunch, BB extremes represent temporary order-book imbalances that self-correct within 60-90 seconds as market makers fade the deviation.

indicators.name: vol_short_36
indicators.purpose: 3-minute realized vol to detect the CURRENT short-term volatility regime. Original used rolling_std(15) on 1-min = 15-min window; compressed to 3 min because we hold 30-120s and need the vol reading to be contemporaneous with the trade — a 15-min window lags too much for a 90-second position.

indicators.name: vol_long_360
indicators.purpose: 30-minute rolling vol as the session baseline ('expected vol at this time of day'). Original used 20-day avg vol by minute, which is unavailable in 5s real-time data. Rolling 30-min window captures the current session's ambient vol regime and provides a stable denominator for vol_ratio without requiring historical day data.

indicators.name: vol_ratio
indicators.purpose: Ratio > 1 signals vol expansion (momentum regime), < 1 signals vol contraction (mean-reversion regime). Direct translation of original's vol_surprise = current_vol / expected_vol — same concept, different baseline source.

indicators.name: bb_120
indicators.purpose: 10-minute Bollinger Bands for mean-reversion entry during lunch. Original used BB(20) on 1-min = 20-min window; compressed to 10 min (120 bars) because our lunch mean-reversion hold is 60-90s and a 10-min band better reflects the current consolidation range rather than a stale 20-min history during a slowly drifting session.

indicators.name: ema_fast_36
indicators.purpose: 3-minute fast EMA for momentum direction. Original EMA(5) on 1-min = 5-min. Scaled to 3 min (36 bars) because at 5s resolution we need a trigger that responds within our max 2-min hold window — a 5-min EMA updates too slowly to signal entries for a 60-90s momentum trade.

indicators.name: ema_slow_120
indicators.purpose: 10-minute slow EMA for trend context. Original EMA(13) on 1-min = 13-min. Kept near-proportional (10 min) because this is a CONTEXT FILTER, not the trade trigger — it should represent the current 10-min trend direction, which aligns with the timeframe our institutional flow hypothesis operates on.

conditions: OPEN/CLOSE period (09:20-10:00 or 14:30-15:25): ema_fast > ema_slow AND vol_ratio > vol_high_ratio (1.15)
LUNCH period (11:30-13:30): close < bb_lower AND vol_ratio < vol_low_ratio (0.85)
AFTERNOON period (13:30-14:30): ema_fast > ema_slow AND vol_ratio in (1.0, vol_high_ratio) AND close > bb_mid
buy_ce.confirmation: All signals fired at 5s bar close; no additional bar confirmation needed given 5s resolution

conditions: OPEN/CLOSE period: ema_fast < ema_slow AND vol_ratio > vol_high_ratio (1.15)
LUNCH period: close > bb_upper AND vol_ratio < vol_low_ratio (0.85)
AFTERNOON period: ema_fast < ema_slow AND vol_ratio in (1.0, vol_high_ratio) AND close < bb_mid
buy_pe.confirmation: Same as buy_ce — fired on bar close

exit.stop_rationale: Momentum trades (open/close): 3 pts — if NIFTY retraces ~6 spot pts (3 option pts at delta 0.5) within 30s of entry, the institutional push has stalled and the trade thesis is wrong. Mean-reversion (lunch): 4 pts stop — BB touches can extend 10-15 spot pts before reversing, so 4 pts gives the trade room while limiting loss to one standard lunch-period swing. Afternoon: 4 pts matching mean-rev risk since direction is less certain.
exit.target_rationale: Momentum trades (open/close): 5 pts — captures ~50% of a typical 30-60s NIFTY momentum push (2-5 option pts per CONVENTIONS.md), giving 1:1.67 R:R at 3 pt stop. Lunch mean-reversion: 7 pts — BB-to-mid reversion on NIFTY covers 15-25 spot pts (7-10 option pts); 7 pts captures the conservative half. Afternoon: 6 pts at midpoint of both regimes.

filters.vix_filter: none — vol regime is self-detected by vol_ratio; VIX not needed as secondary filter
filters.time_filter: strictly period-based: open (09:20-10:00), lunch (11:30-13:30), afternoon (13:30-14:30), close (14:30-15:25); mid-morning (10:00-11:30) excluded to avoid ambiguous regime transitions
filters.volume_filter: none at index level — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY volume is structurally low on 5s bars; vol_ratio implicitly captures activity
filters.trend_filter: EMA alignment acts as trend filter for momentum regimes; BB position acts as range filter for mean-reversion
filters.spread_filter: not applicable — limit orders at close price

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — the U-shape intraday vol pattern is a structural microstructure feature from institutional schedule constraints, not an arbitrage that gets competed away; documented in Indian markets since Sinha (2016)

adaptation_notes: Original traded NIFTY50 stocks on 1-min bars with a 20-day expected vol lookup per minute. Converted to NIFTY index at 5s because: (1) the U-shape is equally present on the index itself, driven by the same institutional order scheduling; (2) we replaced 20-day historical vol lookup with a rolling 30-min baseline (vol_long_360) which is computable in real-time; (3) BB(20,1-min) → BB(120,5s) = 10 min for same time window; (4) EMA(5,1-min) → EMA(36,5s) = 3 min compressed because hold time shrinks from 10-45 min to 30-120s; (5) afternoon vol-expansion trade preserved but simplified — vol_ratio crossing neutral with EMA alignment is the trigger, no RSI needed at 5s since price action is noisy at that scale; (6) mid-morning period (10:00-11:30) excluded because regime is ambiguous (transitioning between open momentum and lunch mean-rev).
weaknesses: Three sub-regimes triple the parameter count and overfitting risk on 12-day backtest window

vol_ratio using rolling 30-min baseline can be slow to adapt on event days when vol spikes suddenly — first 30 min of high-vol event will show artificially high vol_ratio, potentially misfiring momentum signals
Afternoon vol-expansion regime has lowest directional accuracy since vol rising does not guarantee a direction — NIFTY can chop with expanding vol before institutional flow emerges at close
Mid-morning gap (10:00-11:30) means strategy is idle for 90 min mid-session, reducing trade count
